html:
In January 1983 the government of Nigeria ordered undocumented foreigners to leave the country within two weeks. About two million West African migrants were expelled, around half of them from Ghana. The episode is remembered as "Ghana Must Go".

During the oil boom of the 1970s Nigeria's economy drew workers from all over the region, at a time when Ghana's economy was in deep crisis. When oil prices fell, President Shehu Shagari blamed foreigners for unemployment and crime ahead of elections.

The migrants crowded the roads and ports. Many lost their savings and goods, and Ghana, itself in drought and hardship, had to take in a sudden flood of returnees. The cheap checked plastic bags they carried their things in are still called "Ghana Must Go" bags across West Africa.

The expulsion clashed with ECOWAS's promise of free movement. It also echoed Ghana's own expulsion of Nigerians and other foreigners in 1969. Nigeria expelled more migrants in 1985.
